ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, it is known that points O and C are on the same side of line $m$. Draw $\odot O$ intersecting $m$ at points A and B. Connect AC, BC, OA, and OB. If point C is outside of $\odot O$ and $\angle AOB=110^\circ$, then what could be the possible degree of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, let $AC$ intersect $\odot O$ at point $D$, and connect $BD$,

$\because$ $\angle AOB=110^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=55^\circ$,

$\because$ $\angle ADB=\angle C+\angle CBD$,

$\therefore$ $\angle C<55^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $A$ meets the requirements, $BCD$ does not.

Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{\angle C<55^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, line m passes horizontally through circle O and intersects the circle at two points A and B; O is above line m, and C is also above line m and located outside the circle. Segments AC and BC have been connected; among them, AC starts from A, passes through the circle, and then reaches C outside the circle, so AC has a second intersection point D with the circle besides A, and the order is A-D-C. Then reason: Take D as the second intersection point of AC and circle O, and connect BD. Because A, D, and B are all on circle O, and the central angle ∠AOB=110°, the inscribed angle ∠ADB subtending the same arc AB is 110°/2=55°. In triangle BCD, DA is the extension line of DC, therefore ∠ADB is the exterior angle at point D of triangle BCD, so ∠ADB=∠C+∠CBD. Since ∠CBD is a positive angle, ∠C=55°-∠CBD<55°. Therefore the possible values of ∠C satisfy being less than 55°.
